reply.text:
I can't give you a safe-to-mix answer, because that depends on you and on what's in the product. In general, pre-workouts are stimulant-heavy and alcohol is a depressant. The stimulant can make you feel less drunk than you are, and both can dehydrate you and put extra work on your heart. That's why the combination gets a caution on most labels.

For whether it's okay for you, especially with any heart, blood pressure or medication issues, ask a doctor or a dietitian. They can also speak to the specific product, and I can't give you an amount of it.

On the training side, alcohol close to a session hurts recovery and sleep, and sleep is where most of your progress gets made. If you're lifting tonight, I can set up the session or start it for you.
